cross_run_carve_out.derivation_note: DERIVED from the spec: shared-62 hubs and links whose feeds come from BOTH runs. lnk_policy_party is in the shared 62 and is EXCLUDED because the settled map supplies only v2 feeds for it, so there is no cross-run precedence to annotate.
cross_run_carve_out.mechanism_note: The precedence is DETERMINISTIC (v2 > legacy > delta3, BD6 then BD6b) and is NOT changed by the carve-out. 'Emit both values' was proposed and withdrawn: on a single-active attribute two writers into one row per key is LOAD-ORDER-DEPENDENT and strictly worse than a deterministic precedence. The carve-out is HEADER-ONLY -- it names the subordinate writer and its registry so the loss is COUNTABLE.
cross_run_carve_out.why_not_an_overlap_threshold_note: A hub-level business-key-column overlap cannot see the hazard AT ANY THRESHOLD. HUB_PARTY's overlap of 3 is IMD_CODE, PART_ID and RM_CODE, ALL intermediary-side; on the member/customer population the overlap is ZERO. The figure is also unstable: collapsing underscores moves it 3 -> 5, and HUB_PARTY is the only object where normalisation moves it.
cross_run_carve_out.why_declare_note: Chosen on ASYMMETRY: a DECLARED CONFLICT IS RECOVERABLE; A WRONG MERGE IS NOT, AFTER LOAD.

intra_run_fanin.definition_note: GROUP = (satellite, attribute, source_run), MERGED ACROSS TRACKS. WRITER = one distinct (source view, source column) pair, so the same column read through two containers is ONE writer. UNDISCRIMINATED = no instance AND no redundant_of. SINGLE-ACTIVE = data_7.js hist does not contain 'Multi-Active'. A group counts only with 2+ undiscriminated writers. THE UNIT IS THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE between this figure and a per-build-unit one, which reads 228/999.
intra_run_fanin.reconciliation_note: This build measures single-active 180 groups / 825 columns, 6 same-table and 174 cross-table, which REPRODUCES THE MAPPING COUNTERPARTY'S FIGURE EXACTLY. A third figure of 164/765 with 0 same-table was relayed from a different single-active definition; both are recorded and they are NOT reconciled, because the definitions differ and the conclusion -- that essentially the whole surface is CROSS-table -- is the same either way.
intra_run_fanin.three_buckets_note: THREE buckets, not two. A satellite data_7.js does not declare has NO declared history; that is a third state and not a synonym for single-active. Counting it as single-active moved this figure from 180 groups to 228 -- a classification that was fabricated by a dictionary default.
intra_run_fanin.check_collapse_blind_spot_note: check_collapse groups on (table, satellite, attribute, instance, child_key), so it can only flag writers from the SAME table. N writers spread across N different tables produce ZERO violations there. Any previously quoted collapse figure therefore BOUNDS THE SAME-TABLE SUBSET and is not a measurement of the collapse surface; the cross-table population is the larger one and was invisible to that gate on both sides.
intra_run_fanin.severity_note: THE LARGER NON-DETERMINISM, and NO decision taken so far addresses it. Refusing a subordinate RUN cannot touch writers of the SAME run. It is DECLARED in every affected satellite header, at both scopes, and measured by a load-time assertion.
intra_run_fanin.predicate_note: ARBITRARY only among UNDISCRIMINATED writers -- no instance AND no redundant_of. On SAT_PARTY_IDENTITY.'Party Full Name' legacy: 95 writers, 75 separated by a resolved instance, 0 redundant_of, 20 genuinely undiscriminated over 20 distinct tables. A predicate over all 95 would have reported 75 CORRECT rows as defects on a new check's first run.

load_time_assertions.executed_note: dbt is out of scope for this build, so every assertion is EMITTED AND UNRUN. A zero from an unrun assertion is an ABSENCE OF MEASUREMENT, not a clean result.
load_time_assertions.cross_run_reading_note: 0 => no business-key VALUE collided across the two runs' disjoint registries, so the precedence never fired. This is the ONLY self-sufficient answer. >0 => the VALUES collided, which does NOT prove they denote the same ENTITY, so >0 ESCALATES rather than resolves.
load_time_assertions.intra_run_reading_note: 0 rows => every undiscriminated same-run writer agreed on every key. >0 => those are the values this build picked ARBITRARILY.
load_time_assertions.first_case_note: SAT_PARTY_IDENTITY.'Party Full Name' -- 95 legacy writers against 10 v2; 20 of the 95 undiscriminated.

findings.detail: BD1-hashdiff-name -- Hashdiff column is <SAT>_HASHDIFF, not a bare HASHDIFF. WHY: The two originals disagree and s7 cannot decide between two equally-entitled siblings: legacy writes a bare HASHDIFF and never a suffixed one, v2 the exact reverse -- counts taken from build_profile.json sibling.hashdiff_evidence. A bare name collides the moment ONE model computes hashdiffs for more than one satellite, which is what a multi-feed consolidated stage does. s12 already records the bare form as the OPUS spelling implicated in the shared-vault divergence debt. COST: The estate gains a third project using the suffixed form, so a future shared loader spanning this project and legacy must translate one name. Nothing is loaded, so the change costs nothing TODAY; it costs a translation LATER. OVERRULE WITH: hcon_names.hashdiff() -> return 'HASHDIFF'

BD2-legacy-key-archaeology -- Legacy hub key expressions are recovered from health_dv_dbt's EMITTED SQL (read-only), because the legacy half of the map carries zero resolved_key. WHY: Open item R4-builder, proposed_default: 'the build is the authority, not the map'. Without this, EVERY row of the legacy half has no hub key and every shared loader loses its legacy feed -- which would silently convert a consolidation into a v2-only build. Rows per run are taken from build_profile.json map_shape.by_source_run and the loader partition from build_profile.json layer_plan_one_loader. COST: The recovered expression is what legacy's generator EMITTED, not what any map declares, so it cannot be validated against the bundle. The legacy HASH VALUES are NOT reproduced (legacy hashes inside automate_dv macros whose algorithm is INFERRED_NOT_DOCUMENTED); only the BUSINESS KEY EXPRESSION is carried over, re-hashed in the canonical explicit form. Legacy's loaded keys and this project's keys are therefore NOT comparable, which is harmless only because this is a greenfield third project. OVERRULE WITH: hcon_keyrules.LEGACY_ARCHAEOLOGY_ENABLED = False  (legacy feeds then go to UNRESOLVED and every shared loader becomes v2-single-feed)

BD3-no-datatype-catalogue -- Layer-1 casts every source column to varchar. WHY: The pinned bundle contains NO datatype catalogue -- ten files, none a schema. v2's staging carries cast(... as date)/(... as number) because v2's bundle had one. Inventing a type from a column name is a fabricated datum. COST: Every staged column is a string, so downstream date and numeric semantics are lost at layer 1 and any arithmetic must cast again. Hashing is unaffected (every hash operand is cast to varchar anyway). OVERRULE WITH: gen_hcon_staging.TYPE_FOR_COLUMN -- supply a catalogue and return a type

BD4-model-layout -- Models are laid out as v2 does -- models/vault/{hubs,hub_feeds,links,satellites,refs}, models/augmented, models/{staging,stage,unpivot,reject_log} -- NOT under models/automate_dv/. WHY: This project declares NO packages and invokes no automate_dv macro (build directive 6). A directory named automate_dv would assert a dependency that does not exist. COST: STATED PLAINLY: vault_tools/check_vault_alignment.py globs models/automate_dv/*/satellites/*.sql and therefore reaches ZERO files in this layout. That gate's satellite comparison is VACUOUS here and is reported as NOT RUN, never as PASS. check_hcon_payload_naming.py was written to cover the payload-naming half against BOTH originals. Choosing the automate_dv path instead would re-enable the gate at the price of a directory name that lies. OVERRULE WITH: gen_hcon_vault.VAULT_DIR = 'automate_dv/standard'

BD5-source-per-run -- Each run gets its own dbt source name: source('opus_health_legacy_v4', T) and source('opus_health_v2', T). WHY: The two runs share NO table name at all -- per-run table counts and their zero overlap are taken from build_profile.json map_shape -- but they are two different landing areas. One source name would assert they land together. COST: Two source blocks to configure before this project can run. dbt is out of scope here, so nothing resolves them in this build. OVERRULE WITH: gen_hcon_staging.SOURCE_NAME_FOR_RUN -- return one constant

BD6-r8-precedence-order -- Where both runs write one attribute, the declared precedence is V2 FIRST, then legacy: coalesce(v2_value, legacy_value). WHY: v2 is the closed, settled half (profile legacy_half_status.v2_half_token = SETTLED, no Stage-9 blockers) while EVERY pre-stage-6.5 blocker and EVERY target_validity and handoff_outcome_contract finding came from the legacy half, as recorded in build_profile.json open_items. Neither run is declared authoritative ANYWHERE in the bundle, so this is a builder call and not a reading of the map. COST: WHERE LEGACY IS RIGHT AND V2 IS WRONG, THIS PICKS THE WRONG VALUE. The size of the exposure is taken from BUILD_STATUS.json r8 and build_profile.json r8_source_precedence. It is a VALUE choice, never a key change and never RECORD_SOURCE in a key, so it cannot alter grain and is reversible by reload. OVERRULE WITH: hcon_keyrules.R8_PRECEDENCE = ('opus_health_legacy_v4', 'opus_health_v2')

BD7-refuse-not-coin -- A child-key leg that is NAMED but whose value is absent or of the wrong kind is REFUSED, and the satellite is built WITHOUT that leg, with the refusal in its header and in the unresolved-grain register. WHY: Build directive 3, and s5.7: the map is not corrected here. The THREE legacy sub-populations -- nothing-at-all, leg-named-but-no-value, and leg-named-with-a-value-of-the-wrong-kind -- are counted in BUILD_STATUS.json and in reports/declared_unresolved_grain_hcon.json. None of the three yields a discriminator without inventing one. COST: Those satellites LOSE GRAIN: rows that differ only in the refused leg collapse onto one hash key. The collapse is DECLARED and countable rather than hidden, which is the only property available here -- the alternative is a fabricated discriminator that no gate can see. OVERRULE WITH: hcon_keyrules.REFUSE_UNRESOLVED_LEGS = False (and then every collapsed row is a silent data loss)

BD8-ordinal-legs-are-not-hub-grade -- A renumbering-ordinal leg is built when the map supplies its value, and its instability is stated in the satellite header; it is never synthesised. WHY: The unstable legs are named in build_profile.json renumbering_ordinals: Contact Priority Order, Coverage Sequence, Role Sequence, Active Sequence Number. Each changes when a sibling row is added or removed, so none is hub-grade -- a renumbering ordinal breaks a child key exactly as it breaks a hub key. COST: A source renumbering rewrites history on the affected satellites. Declared in the header so the instability is visible before load, not after. OVERRULE WITH: hcon_keyrules.ORDINAL_LEGS_ALLOWED = False (those legs then refuse)

BD6b-delta3-ranked-last -- The third run, opus_health_delta3, is ranked LAST in the declared precedence: coalesce(v2_value, legacy_value, delta3_value). WHY: MEASURED, not preferred. Delta 3 co-writes 79 of the 594 (satellite, attribute) pairs in the merged map -- 34 with legacy alone, 33 with both, 12 with v2 alone -- so the rank FIRES and is a real value choice. BD6 ranked v2 above legacy because v2 is the SETTLED half, NOT because it is newer; delta 3's settledness is established NOWHERE in its bundle, so there is no basis on BD6's own stated principle to rank it above either existing run. Ranking it first would change the chosen value on all 79 pairs the 115 build already emits, including Party Full Name, Date Of Birth and Identification Number -- a change this consolidation was instructed not to introduce. COST: WHERE DELTA 3 IS RIGHT AND THE EXISTING WINNER IS WRONG, THIS PICKS THE WRONG VALUE, on those 79 pairs. It is a VALUE choice, never a key change and never RECORD_SOURCE in a key, so it cannot alter grain and is reversible by reload. Delta 3's OWN 40 pairs, which no other run writes, are unaffected by the rank. OVERRULE WITH: hcon_keyrules.R8_PRECEDENCE -- move 'opus_health_delta3' earlier in the tuple (first = delta 3 wins every shared attribute)

anchor_not_keyed_on_this_view_in_legacy_sql: 251 occurrence(s). UNIT = one refusal record; POPULATION = build_artifacts/hcon_spec.json -> unresolved. DISPOSITION REFUSE_AND_DECLARE / STATUS AWAITING_COUNTERPARTY / ATTRIBUTION mapper-ratified. All of them refused now; a re-homing pass is promised. THE COUNTERPARTY'S OWN DIAGNOSIS, which is the valuable part: their Stage 6.5 validated anchor == parent(satellite), a MODEL constraint, and never asked whether the VIEW CAN KEY THAT HUB, a SOURCE constraint. THE LARGER NON-DETERMINISM, AND NO DECISION TAKEN SO FAR ADDRESSES IT. The cross-run carve-out and the declared source precedence both operate BETWEEN runs. The arbitrary pick is WITHIN a run: several views of ONE run write one attribute, the map declares no precedence among them, and max() keeps one. Refusing a subordinate RUN cannot touch it -- the 95 legacy writers of SAT_PARTY_IDENTITY.'Party Full Name' are all the same run. MEASURED, unit = a (satellite, attribute, source_run) group of UNDISCRIMINATED writers (no instance AND no redundant_of), writer = one distinct (source view, source column) pair: single-active 206 group(s) / 894 column(s), of which CROSS-table 200/873 and SAME-table 6/21; multi-active 126/909; satellites with NO declared history in data_7.js 48/184. This build's single-active figure REPRODUCES THE COUNTERPARTY'S MEASUREMENT EXACTLY. A third figure of 164 groups / 765 columns with 0 same-table was relayed from a different single-active definition; both are recorded and NOT reconciled, because the conclusion is the same either way -- essentially the whole surface is CROSS-table. The counterparty has taken the 174 cross-table groups. DECLARED, not resolved: choosing among same-run writers would invent an authority the map does not provide.

check_collapse CANNOT SEE THE LARGER POPULATION, and this invalidates how its figure has been quoted on both sides. It groups on (table, satellite, attribute, instance, child_key), so it can only flag two writers from the SAME TABLE. N writers spread across N DIFFERENT tables produce ZERO violations. MEASURED: of the 206 single-active fan-in groups, only 6 are same-table. So the long-quoted 'violations, all pre-existing' figure BOUNDS THE SAME-TABLE SUBSET and is NOT a measurement of the collapse surface; the cross-table population is the larger one and was invisible to that gate on both sides. Legacy collapse totals remain NOT_MEASURABLE, never zero.

BD6-CARVED-OUT (builder-overruled-by-mapper). Scope: 16 shared objects written by BOTH runs -- the 14 shared hubs plus LNK_PARTY_ROLE -- DERIVED from the spec, not retyped. lnk_policy_party is in the shared 62 and EXCLUDED because the settled map supplies only v2 feeds for it. The MECHANISM is unchanged: the declared source precedence stays deterministic (v2 > legacy). 'Emit both values' was proposed and WITHDRAWN -- on a single-active attribute two writers into one row per key is load-order-dependent and strictly worse. The carve-out is HEADER-ONLY: it NAMES the subordinate writer and its registry so the loss is countable. An overlap THRESHOLD was rejected as the instrument because it cannot see the hazard at any value: HUB_PARTY's overlap of 3 is IMD_CODE, PART_ID and RM_CODE, ALL intermediary-side, while on the member/customer population it is ZERO, and collapsing underscores moves the figure 3 -> 5. Scope chosen on ASYMMETRY: a declared conflict is RECOVERABLE, a wrong merge is NOT after load.

LOAD-TIME ASSERTIONS (builder). 97 emitted, 14 cross-run collision and 82 intra-run arbitrariness, in models/assertions/, ALL UNRUN -- dbt is out of scope, so a zero from any of them is an ABSENCE OF MEASUREMENT, not a clean result. They exist because both questions are DATA questions: whether a business-key VALUE ever collides across the two runs' disjoint registries is unanswerable statically, and so is whether same-run writers ever disagree. Reading the cross-run result: 0 is the ONLY self-sufficient answer; >0 proves the VALUES collided and NOT that they denote the same ENTITY, so it ESCALATES rather than resolves. The intra-run predicate is restricted to UNDISCRIMINATED writers -- over all writers it would have reported 75 of 95 CORRECT rows as defects on SAT_PARTY_IDENTITY.'Party Full Name' alone, and a gate that over-accuses gets switched off and then protects nothing.
